newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Capex contributes to Australia GDP, outlook firms.
newsitem.headline: Capex contributes to Australia GDP, outlook firms.

text.p: Australian capital expenditure figures have boosted the outlook for March quarter gross domestic product, with plant and equipment spending contributing 0.3 or 0.4 percentage points to quarterly growth.
Analysts said a rise in spending on buildings and structures pointed to a GDP contribution from overall business investment greater than 0.3 or 0.4 points.
Before the capex data was issued earlier on Tuesday economists had typically expected a business investment contribution to GDP of 0.3 percentage points.
Capital expenditure estimates for the quarters back to December 1995 were not significantly revised.
The Australian Bureau of Statistics divides capital expenditure into two categories but uses only one of them, plant and equipment, directly in GDP data.
Economists say the other component, building and structures, is not a bad indicator of the direction for the equivalent item in GDP but not magnitude.
In the March quarter, seasonally adjusted plant and equipment spending rose by A$388 million in the 1989/90 currency of GDP data -- 0.35 percent of GDP.
Buildings and structures rose another A$279 million, implying further upward contribution.
"It (the capital spending data) is above consensus, so overall expectations of GDP should be revised a little higher," said HongKong Bank economist Anthony Thompson.
Thompson thought overall business investment might now contribute 0.5 percentage point to quarterly GDP growth.
AMP Society chief economist Shane Oliver said he would now probably revise up his March quarter GDP growth forecast.
"We were at 0.9 percent for GDP for the quarter, and we might be looking to revise it up to 1.0 percent," he said.
"The only caution would be that there is still some data to come, particularly for net exports and stocks figures."

The bureau's March quarter GDP estimates is due to be issued on June 4. Although many of the so-called partial indicators have now been published, some of the most influential are yet to come, notably business inventories or stocks.

Business investment is a component of the expenditure-based estimate of GDP (GDP-E) which is averaged with income and production-based estimates (GDP-I and -P) to produce GDP-A, the focus of economic policy.
